newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq can export 2.5 mln bpd of oil now -official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq can export 2.5 mln bpd of oil now -official.

text.p: Iraq is capable of exporting up to 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil and is ready to resume sales under the "oil-for-food" deal with the United Nations, a senior official said in remarks published on Sunday.

"Iraq can from today export 2.5 million bpd of crude oil which can be increased to three million bpd if only minor technical requirements are made availble," Undersecretary of Oil Taha Hamoud, told the official al-Qadissiya newspaper.
"We are ready to resume oil exports (under the oil deal)," he said.

The oil-for-food deal, which went into effect last December, allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil every 180 days to buy food and medicine to help offset the effects of sanctions in place since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The pact was renewed by the U.N. Security Council for another six months from June 8. But the exports have been held up pending U.N. approval of an Iraqi procurement and distribution plan.
